messages:
maria: Quick question — how should the smoke prober surface tokenizer / signature mismatches to the bench? We had 3 model ingests in the last hour fail at the validator step and it wasn't obvious which field triggered it.
aj: For fast triage I want a single, small failure code that points to a prescriptive next step. e.g. TOKENIZER_MISMATCH -> run `tools/token-diff --gold <model>` and the ingest UI should link to that run.
devon: Agreed. Also we should avoid noisy failures. If it's a minor tokenization variance (<=1% token diff on golden set) we should flag as WARN not FAIL. Only hard fails block admission.
sasha: Tradeoff: WARNs let bad models slip through. If downstream runtime relies on exact vocab mapping (legacy ops) WARNs are dangerous. Maybe add a per-model confidence-level on the descriptor: `strict_tokenizer: true|false`.
maria: Good point. Could we default to strict=false for new open models and strict=true for models that opt into enterprise runtime? That maps to Dedicated/Private needs.
linh: Implementation proposal: prober returns an array of signals with a top-level status. Example payload (simplified):
```json
{"status":"FAIL","signals":[{"id":"tokenizer_mismatch","severity":"high","diff_pct":3.2,"how_to_fix":"use-tokenizer-compat shim","examples":["gold_text -> token list","model_text -> token list"]}]}
```
Keep top-level status conservative (FAIL if any high severity).
aj: Love that. Also include quickperf metrics: seqlen-distribution, median-latency-ms, kv-cache-hit-rate. Ops wants a 95th latency baseline in the report.
ci-bot: ingest-build 4999 completed — prober ran on 3 models: mdl-x (WARN), mdl-y (FAIL), mdl-z (PASS). Logs: https://ci/reports/4999
devon: On the bench side: when we see WARN we should auto-queue a deeper bench (30min) and mark for human review. FAIL should trigger immediate rollback of the admission attempt and post a short checklist to the model owner.
sasha: Interface boundary question: do we let the bench pull artifacts from prober (golden diffs) or should prober publish a signed artifact bundle to the registry that bench then pulls? I prefer signed bundles to make runs reproducible.
maria: Signed bundles + minimal JSON summary in the prober response sounds good. Bench can fetch bundle by artifact_id. Avoids duplication.
linh: One more thing: coldstart behavior. If a model's warmup path misses (e.g. KV cache priming not matching runtime workload) we get weird tail latencies. Prober should include a warmup-sim sample and a flag `warmup_recommended_steps`.
aj: For quantized variants we need an extra compatibility check: runtime kernel availability. If the runtime cannot map ops for a quantized binary we should surface KERNEL_UNSUPPORTED with list of missing ops.
devon: That suggests the prober needs a small runtime shim (local kernel probe) that runs only signature/kernel extraction, not full inference. Lightweight but deterministic.
sasha: Ops-wise, propose policy:
- PASS: auto-accept to shadow (no traffic) for 24h, run golden regression nightly.
- WARN: auto-schedule deep bench + require owner ack within 48h.
- FAIL: block admission, owner must fix and resubmit.
maria: Can we add a graded canary stage where a model that passes but has flaky seqlen tail enters canary with reduced concurrency? Helps catch tail regressions.
aj: Yes — add `canary_policy` field to descriptor with concurrency_limit and traffic_pct. Default is null.
linh: On observability: bench reports should include a golden-diff histogram and an example pair where model output diverges the most. Debugging time plummets if we have one concrete counterexample.
devon: One last UX ask: ingest UI should present the single-line failure summary and a 1-click button to re-run prober with verbose logs. Saves cycles.
maria: OK next steps: linh will draft prober response spec (signals + artifact id + perf metrics). aj will sketch ingest UI changes. devon will wire bench auto-queue logic. Sasha will document policy table (PASS/WARN/FAIL). I'll follow up with an RFC update next week. :thumbsup:
